# Adjudication Task — Chapter 542

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃542화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|걸음걸이는 그 사람의 성향을 알 수 있는 중요한 지표 중 하나다.
  6|
  7|특히 무림인의 경우에는 생각 이상으로 많은 정보가 걸음걸이에 담겨 있다.
  8|
  9|우악스러운 힘을 바탕으로 무공을 펼치는 이의 걸음을 무겁고 거칠다.
 10|
 11|반면 유려한 무공을 익혔거나, 살수와 같은 특정한 경우에는 발소리도 잘 들리지 않을 만큼 은밀하고 가볍다.
 12|
 13|그런 의미에서 지금 계단을 올라오고 있는 누군가의 걸음걸이는, 자신의 존재를 알리다 못해 소리를 지르고 있다 해도 과언이 아니었다.
 14|
 15|쿵, 쿵, 쿵.
 16|
 17|‘사운드 보소.’
 18|
 19|평범한 사람이라면 듣는 것만으로도 심장이 내려앉을 만큼 육중한 소음.
 20|
 21|보보(步步)마다 제법 단단하게 설계되어 있는 계단이 삐걱거리고 미세한 진동이 전해진다.
 22|
 23|어느새 옆구리에 찬 호리병을 꺼내 술을 홀짝이고 있던 적천강이 심각한 표정으로 입을 열었다.
 24|
 25|“암천. 그놈들이 하다 하다 이제는 사람으로 괴물까지 만드는군. 도대체 무슨 술수를 쓴 거지?”
 26|
 27|“예?”
 28|
 29|순간 뭔 소린가 했네.
 30|
 31|곧장 적천강의 말을 이해한 내가 손을 내저었다.
 32|
 33|“그, 말씀하시는 중에 죄송한데 지금 올라오는 놈은 암천 아닌데요.”
 34|
 35|“음. 그래도 걱정할 만한 수준의 상대는 아니니, 문을 열고 들어오는 즉시 네 녀석이 때려눕히거라. 무림맹에 던져 주면 뭐라도 나오겠지.”
 36|
 37|“……아니, 암천 아니라니까요. 그리고 문은 노야께서 이미 박살 내셨으면서 뭘.”
 38|
 39|“뭣이?”
 40|
 41|눈이 화등잔만 해진 적천강이 침까지 튀겨가며 말했다.
 42|
 43|“그럼 지금 올라오고 있는 저놈이 순수한 인간이란 말이냐?”
 44|
 45|“놀랍게도, 자연산입니다.”
 46|
 47|“허어, 인생 오래 살고 봐야 할 일이로고. 그런데 느껴지는 기파가 그리 정순하지는 않던데.”
 48|
 49|응급환자를 내려보내고 돌아온 혁무진이 일양노의 피가 흥건하게 묻은 손바닥을 바짓단에 문지르며 대답했다.
 50|
 51|“이야, 역시 적 대협이십니다. 사마외도를 단번에 알아보시는군요.”
 52|
 53|“사마외도?”
 54|
 55|“예. 흑룡마문(黑龍魔門)의 소문주와 그 수하지요.”
 56|
 57|커다란 소음에 가려져 있어 잘 들리지 않았을 뿐, 처음부터 인기척은 하나가 아니라 둘이었다.
 58|
 59|그리고 마침내 두 사람이 적천강의 난입으로 뻥 뚫려 버린 문 너머로 모습을 드러냈다.
 60|
 61|“무림말학 사마표가 화왕 적천강 대협을 뵙습니다.”
 62|
 63|훤칠한 키에 잘생긴 얼굴의 사내. 그를 마주하자마자 입안이 모래를 씹은 것처럼 까끌거린다.
 64|
 65|문득 머릿속을 스쳐 지나가는 세 글자 때문이다.
 66|
 67|‘정혼자.’
 68|
 69|내 생각을 아는지 모르는지, 적천강을 향해 포권을 취한 사마표가 옆에 멀뚱멀뚱 서 있는 덩어리를 툭 쳤다.
 70|
 71|“뭐 하느냐. 어서 인사 올리지 않고.”
 72|
 73|별호와 이름이 찰떡처럼 어울리는 호거아(虎巨兒) 태산이 꾸벅 허리를 굽혔다.
 74|
 75|“반갑다. 태산이. 화왕 봤다.”
 76|
 77|“…….”
 78|
 79|신박한 인사법일세.
 80|
 81|슬쩍 적천강의 표정을 보니 화왕이 아니라 염라대왕을 보여 주고 싶은 기색이 역력하다.
 82|
 83|그런 낌새를 눈치챈 듯 사마표가 신속하게 부연설명을 덧붙였다.
 84|
 85|“적 대협께서도 짐작하셨겠지만, 어휘력이 부족해서 이게 최선입니다.”
 86|
 87|“……그렇다면 어쩔 수 없긴 한데.”
 88|
 89|적천강이 떨떠름한 얼굴로 중얼거렸다.
 90|
 91|“별 해괴한 놈을 다 보겠군. 그래, 노부도 네놈 봤느니라.”
 92|
 93|“헤헤.”
 94|
 95|순진하게 웃은 태산이 대뜸 쌍따봉을 날렸다.
 96|
 97|“화왕. 강하다. 태산이. 강자 좋다. 반갑다.”
 98|
 99|“오, 오냐. 노부도 반갑다.”
100|
101|“그런데 태산이. 배고프다.”
102|
103|“뭐, 뭐라?”
104|
105|“저거 먹고 싶다. 화왕 허락해 주면 고맙다.”
106|
107|식탐이 가득한 눈빛은 어느새 우리의 어깨너머를 향하고 있었다.
108|
109|탁자 위에 놓인 다과의 존재를 깨달은 적천강이 엉겁결에 고개를 끄덕였다.
110|
111|“그, 그래라.”
112|
113|“와! 다과! 태산이, 잘 먹겠습니다!”
114|
115|쿵! 콰직!
116|
117|객잔 주인이 피눈물을 흘리겠구만.
118|
119|평범한 사람이라고는 볼 수 없는 엄청난 덩치가 그나마 남아 있던 문짝의 잔해를 박살 내며 돌격한다.
120|
121|기다렸다는 듯 탁자 위의 모든 것을 쓸어 담는 태산의 모습을 멍하니 바라보던 적천강이 중얼거렸다.
122|
123|“노부가 너무 오래 살았나.”
124|
125|아무리 적천강이라고 해도 당황하지 않을 수 없는 모양이다.
126|
127|하긴, 지금까지 화왕이라는 두 글자만 대면 설설 기는 사람들만 상대해 왔으니 그럴 만도 했다.
128|
129|아마 청풍을 제외하고는 처음으로 등장하는 강적의 등장이 아닐까.
130|
131|‘뭐, 그건 그렇다 치고.’
132|
133|뒤통수를 긁적인 나는 사마표를 위아래로 훑었다.
134|
135|“그래서. 여기에는 무슨 일로?”
136|
137|“중요한 용무가 있어서. 괜찮다면 안으로 들어가서 이야기하면 좋겠는데.”
138|
139|“아니, 별로 괜찮지 않아서 그래.”
140|
141|사마표가 어깨를 으쓱해 보였다.
142|
143|“예의상 물어본 건데, 역시 평범하진 않군. 자네도 사마외도에 악감정이 있었나?”
144|
145|“악감정이라기보다는…….”
146|
147|제기랄. 막상 이렇게 나오니 뭐라 할 말이 없다.
148|
149|녀석과는 겨우 한 번 만난 것이 고작이지만 첫인상이 그리 나쁘지도 않았고, 내가 틈만 나면 사마외도 척결과 정파 짱짱맨을 외치는 골수주의자도 아니니까.
150|
151|그리고 그건 적천강도 크게 다르지 않았다.
152|
153|“거기 서서 뭔 짓거리들이냐? 정분났어?”
154|
155|적천강까지 저리 말하니 딱히 거절할 이유가 없다. 고민을 끝마친 나는 사마표를 향해 턱짓했다.
156|
157|“젠장, 들어오든가.”
158|
159|“고맙군. 감사합니다, 적 대협.”
160|
161|정중한 인사와 함께 안으로 들어오는 사마표의 모습에 적천강이 고개를 끄덕였다.
162|
163|“어린놈이 제법 싸가지는 있구나. 아니면 음흉한 핏줄을 이어받은 건가?”
164|
165|순간 멈칫한 사마표가 빙긋 웃었다.
166|
167|“아마 후자일 겁니다. 그나저나 제 아버님을 기억하고 계시는군요.”
168|
169|“네놈의 얼굴을 보기 전까지는 잊고 있었지. 흑야왕(黑夜王), 그놈의 소싯적 모습을 쏙 빼다 박았군.”
170|
171|흑야왕 사마공.
172|
173|사마표의 아버지이자, 지금의 흑룡마문을 만든 입지전적인 인물이다.
174|
175|별호만 보면 십왕(十王) 중 한 사람이라고 생각하기 쉽지만. 궁기방을 통해 알게 된 정보에 따르면 십왕과는 아무런 연관도 없었다.
176|
177|‘녹림맹주인 녹림투왕(綠林鬪王)과 용봉표국의 표왕(鏢王)처럼.’
178|
179|그들 역시 범접할 수 없는 무위를 지닌 초절정 고수였지만, 십왕이라는 전설의 한 자락으로 인정받기에는 무리였다.
180|
181|사파 무림에서 손꼽히는 고수이자 흑룡마문의 문주인 흑야왕 사마공 역시 같은 맥락으로 그러한 별호를 얻었다고 했다.
182|
183|“그나저나……”
184|
185|사마표를 지그시 바라보던 적천강이 문득 미간을 찌푸렸다.
186|
187|“흑야왕에게 이렇게 젊은 아들놈이 있을 줄은 몰랐는데.”
188|
189|“위로 형님 일곱과 누이 아홉이 있습니다. 제가 막내지요.”
190|
191|“허, 정력도왕이 들으면 울고 가겠군. 그럼 네 녀석이 소문주렸다.”
192|
193|사마표의 눈동자가 살짝 커졌다.
194|
195|“그렇습니다만, 그건 어찌…….”
196|
197|“뻔하지 않느냐.”
198|
199|코웃음 친 적천강이 말을 이었다.
200|
201|“흑야왕, 그놈 성격이라면 능히 그러고도 남지. 자질이 뒷받침된다면 다른 자식들은 순장(殉葬)해도 신경 쓰지 않을 놈이니까.”
202|
203|“…….”
204|
205|“기억하는 모습과 크게 달라지지 않은 모양이군. 도무지 속내를 알 수 없는 놈이었지. 여우처럼 약삭빠르고, 독사처럼 교활했어.”
206|
207|면전에 대고 패드립 박는 클라스 봐라. 가슴이 웅장해진다.
208|
209|사마표의 자질을 인정한다는 속뜻이 있긴 하지만 결국 패드립은 패드립. 나는 아빠 욕에 발끈한 효자 아들이 일을 벌이기 전에 불쑥 입을 열었다.
210|
211|“그래서, 무슨 일이야?”
212|
213|“……흠. 글쎄.”
214|
215|생각을 알 수 없는 오묘한 표정을 짓고 있던 사마표가 품에서 무언가를 꺼내 들었다.
216|
217|무림에서는 제법 비싼 취급을 받는 종이. 그리고 종이의 최상단에 적힌 문구가 단번에 눈에 띈다.
218|
219|
220|
221|★무명 소졸이었던 내가, 이룡각에서는 무림 영웅?!★
222|
223|
224|
225|탁자 위에 놓인 종이를 빤히 내려다보던 나는 턱을 문질렀다.
226|
227|“제법 눈에 익은데.”
228|
229|사마표가 피식 웃었다.
230|
231|“눈에 익을 수밖에.”
232|
233|“누가 생각했는지는 모르겠지만, 천재적이야.”
234|
235|“파격적이기도 하고.”
236|
237|툭.
238|
239|사마표의 길쭉한 손가락이 종이의 한 부분을 짚었다.
240|
241|혁무진이 악필로 휘갈겨 쓴 모집요건(募集要件).
242|
243|바로 그 아래에 존재하는 여러 항목 중에서도 손가락은 정확히 한 곳을 가리키고 있었다.
244|
245|
246|
247|＃성별 및 출신 문파 안 따지고
248|
249|
250|
251|부드러운 목소리가 이어졌다.
252|
253|“특히 이 부분이 마음에 들더군.”
254|
255|“그래서?”
256|
257|“지원하겠네. 이룡각에.”
258|
259|내심 짐작은 하고 있었지만, 이렇게 직접 들으니 기분이 복잡미묘하다.
260|
261|잠시 고민하던 나는 입맛을 다셨다.
262|
263|“이유는?”
264|
265|“노래를 듣는 순간 느낌이 오더군. 딱 내가 원하던 곳이지 뭔가.”
266|
267|“응. 헛소리.”
268|
269|웃기지도 않는 이야기다.
270|
271|성공 시대가 시작되고, 찾는 문파가 많아지고, 인생이 달라질 거라는 노래 가사는 사마표에게 해당하지 않는 이야기니까.
272|
273|흑룡마문은 사파 무림에서도 세 손가락 안에 드는 힘을 지닌 문파.
274|
275|설령 사마표가 소문주가 아니었다 해도 흑야왕의 핏줄로 태어난 이상 어느 정도의 부귀영화는 보장된 것이나 다름없었다.
276|
277|‘그런 놈이 이룡각에 들어오길 청한다?’
278|
279|아무리 정파 골수분자들이 피켓 들고 시위를 벌여도 사마표는 무림맹에서 한 자리를 차지할 수 있는 놈이다.
280|
281|나는 팔짱을 낀 채로 사마표를 지그시 응시했다.
282|
283|“농담이라면 재미없는데.”
284|
285|“다행이군. 전부 진담이거든.”
286|
287|“헛소리 집어치우고. 진짜 이유가 뭐야?”
288|
289|“이유를 대야 한다는 건 방에 적혀 있던 내용에 없었네만.”
290|
291|“가라. 멀리 안 나간다.”
292|
293|사마표가 어쩔 수 없다는 듯이 어깨를 으쓱해 보였다.
294|
295|“이룡각에 들어간다면, 사마외도라는 꼬리표를 뗄 수 있지 않을까 싶어서.”
296|
297|“딱히 떼고 싶어 하는 것 같지는 않던데.”
298|
299|“정말 그렇게 보이나?”
300|
301|“믿음이 안 가는 게 사실이지.”
302|
303|“그렇다면 어쩔 수 없군. 그럼 이참에 허심탄회하게 털어놓겠네.”
304|
305|“털어놔. 개 털리기 싫으면.”
306|

[P82]
His epithet made him sound like one of the Ten Kings, but according to Gung Gibang, he had nothing to do with them.

[P83]
*Just like the Green Forest Battle King, leader of the Green Forest Alliance, and the Escort King of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.*

[P84]
They were Supreme Peak masters whose martial prowess was beyond most people’s reach. That still wasn’t enough to make them part of the legend of the Ten Kings.

[P85]
The Black Night King was one of the greatest masters of the unorthodox faction and the Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate. He’d earned his epithet in much the same way.

[P86]
“Still……”

[P87]
Jeok Cheongang studied Sama Pyo, then frowned.

[P88]
“I didn’t know the Black Night King had a son so young.”

[P89]
“I have seven older brothers and nine older sisters. I’m the youngest.”

[P90]
“Hah. The Virility Saber King would weep if he heard that. So you’re the Young Sect Leader.”

[P91]
Sama Pyo’s eyes widened slightly.

[P92]
“I am, but how did you—”

[P93]
“Isn’t it obvious?”

[P94]
Jeok Cheongang snorted.

[P95]
“That’s exactly the sort of thing the Black Night King would do. If you had the talent, he wouldn’t care if all his other children were buried alive with him.”

[P96]
“……”

[P97]
“He hasn’t changed much, then. You could never tell what that man was thinking. Sly as a fox and cunning as a viper.”

[P98]
There he went, insulting the man’s father to his face. My heart swelled.

[P99]
The insult implied he recognized Sama Pyo’s talent, but it was still an insult. Before the dutiful son could take offense and start something, I cut in.

[P100]
“So what brings you here?”

[P101]
“……Hmm. Well.”

[P102]
Sama Pyo’s expression was hard to read. He reached inside his robe and took something out.

[P103]
Paper—a fairly expensive commodity in Murim. The words at the top caught my eye at once.

[P104]
> ★I Was a Nameless Foot Soldier, but in the Two Dragons Pavilion, I’m a Murim Hero?!★

[P105]
I stared at the sheet he’d laid on the table and rubbed my chin.

[P106]
“This looks familiar.”

[P107]
Sama Pyo gave a quiet laugh.

[P108]
“It would.”

[P109]
“I don’t know who came up with it, but they’re a genius.”

[P110]
“It’s rather bold, too.”

[P111]
Tap.

[P112]
Sama Pyo’s long finger came down on one part of the sheet: the recruitment requirements Hyuk Mujin had scrawled in his terrible handwriting. Of all the lines beneath them, he pointed to one in particular.

[P113]
> \# Gender and sect affiliation don’t matter

[P114]
“I especially like this part,” he said.

[P115]
“So?”

[P116]
“I’d like to apply. To the Two Dragons Pavilion.”

[P117]
I’d suspected as much, but hearing him say it still left me with mixed feelings.

[P118]
I thought for a moment, then clicked my tongue.

[P119]
“Why?”

[P120]
“The moment I heard the song, I knew. It’s exactly the place I’ve been looking for.”

[P121]
“Yeah. Bullshit.”

[P122]
That wasn’t even funny.

[P123]
The song promised a new era of success, more sects seeking you out, and a changed life. None of that applied to Sama Pyo.

[P124]
The Black Dragon Demon Gate was one of the three most powerful sects in the unorthodox martial world. Even if Sama Pyo hadn’t been its Young Sect Leader, being born the Black Night King’s son all but guaranteed him wealth and status.

[P125]
*And he wants to join the Two Dragons Pavilion?*

[P126]
No matter how many orthodox diehards waved picket signs in protest, Sama Pyo could secure himself a position in the Murim Alliance.

[P127]
I folded my arms and stared at him.

[P128]
“If this is a joke, it’s not funny.”

[P129]
“Fortunately, I’m serious.”

[P130]
“Cut the bullshit. What’s the real reason?”

[P131]
“The notice didn’t say I had to give one.”

[P132]
“Then get lost. I won’t see you out.”

[P133]
Sama Pyo shrugged as though he had no choice.

[P134]
“I thought joining the Two Dragons Pavilion might let me shed the label of the unorthodox faction.”

[P135]
“You don’t seem all that eager to shed it.”

[P136]
“Is that really how I seem?”

[P137]
“I don’t trust you.”

[P138]
“Fair enough. Then I’ll speak frankly.”

[P139]
“Go on. Unless you want the shit beaten out of you.”

[P140]
Sama Pyo gave a quiet laugh. Then his expression hardened.

[P141]
His low voice reached my ears.

[P142]
“I intend to use you for my own benefit. Depending on the circumstances, you could be useful to me in any number of ways.”

[P143]
A heavy silence fell.

[P144]
Even Taishan stopped chewing. Hyuk Mujin looked between Sama Pyo and me, his eyes wide.

[P145]
Then someone broke the silence.

[P146]
“What an interesting fellow.”

[P147]
Jeok Cheongang was watching Sama Pyo with an expression I couldn’t read. Was he amused or angry? He turned to me.

[P148]
“What do you think?”

[P149]
I considered it for a moment.

[P150]
“He makes quite an impression. I doubt this is his first interview.”

[P151]
“Will you take him?”

[P152]
“Hard to say.”

[P153]
Black Dragon Saber Sama Pyo. I couldn’t tell how much of what he’d said was a joke and how much he meant.

[P154]
But one thing was certain.

[P155]
*He’s interesting.*

[P156]
Tap. Tap.

[P157]
For a moment, the only sound was my fingers against the table. I gathered my thoughts and looked Sama Pyo straight in the eye.

[P158]
“Let’s make one thing clear first.”

[P159]
“By all means.”

[P160]
“If you try anything—”

[P161]
“Summary execution,” Sama Pyo said before I could finish. “I’ll remember.”

[P162]
“Huh. Straight to the point.”

[P163]
“It’s only natural. Are we done, then?”

[P164]
“You haven’t been accepted. I’m just considering you. Go home for today.”

[P165]
“Very well.”

[P166]
What the hell was he really after?

[P167]
I watched Sama Pyo and Taishan prepare to leave, my curiosity only growing. Then I remembered one important thing.

[P168]
“And one more thing.”

[P169]
“……?”

[P170]
“You’re paying for that guy’s food.”

[P171]
“……!”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)

* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

“Well, you do see some things if you live long enough. The qi I sense from him isn’t particularly pure, though.”

[P21]
Hyuk Mujin had returned after taking the injured man downstairs. Wiping his palm, still slick with Old Man Ilyang’s blood, on his trouser leg, he answered.

[P22]
“Ah, as expected of Great Hero Jeok. You recognized demonic, heterodox arts at once.”

[P23]
“Demonic, heterodox arts?”

[P24]
“Yes. The Young Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate and his subordinate.”

[P25]
The thundering footsteps had drowned out the other sound, but there had been two people coming up from the start.

[P26]

[P27]
“This junior, Sama Pyo, pays his respects to Great Hero Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King.”

[P28]
Tall and handsome. The moment I saw him, my mouth felt as gritty as if I’d bitten into sand.

[P29]
Three words had flashed through my mind.

[P30]
*Former fiancé.*

[P31]
Whether he knew what I was thinking or not, Sama Pyo clasped his hands in greeting to Jeok Cheongang, then nudged the hulking figure standing blankly beside him.

[P32]
“What are you doing? Pay your respects.”

[P33]
Tiger Giant Child Taishan, whose name and epithet fit him perfectly, bent at the waist.

[P34]
“Nice to meet. Taishan saw Fire King.”

[P35]
“……”

[P36]
That was a new one.

[P37]

[P38]
Sama Pyo seemed to notice and quickly explained.

[P39]
“As you may have guessed, his vocabulary is limited. That’s the best he can do.”

[P40]
“……Well, if that’s the case.”

[P41]
Jeok Cheongang muttered, looking less than pleased.

[P42]
“I’ve seen some strange fellows in my time. Fine. This old man has seen you too.”

[P43]
“Heh heh.”

[P44]
Taishan smiled innocently and gave him two thumbs up.

[P45]
“Fire King. Strong. Taishan likes strong people. Nice to meet.”

[P46]
“Y-Yes. This old man is pleased to meet you too.”

[P47]
“But Taishan. Hungry.”

[P48]
“W-What?”

[P49]
“Want to eat that. If Fire King says yes, Taishan grateful.”

[P50]
His hungry eyes had already moved past our shoulders.

[P51]
Jeok Cheongang spotted the refreshments on the table and nodded before he quite knew what he was doing.

[P52]
“G-Go ahead.”

[P53]
“Wow! Refreshments! Taishan thanks you for the food!”

[P54]
Thud! Crack!

[P55]
The innkeeper was going to weep tears of blood.

[P56]
The enormous man charged forward, smashing what remained of the door on his way in. As though he’d been waiting for permission, Taishan swept up everything on the table. Jeok Cheongang watched him in a daze.

[P57]
“Have I lived too long?”

[P58]
Even Jeok Cheongang couldn’t help being taken aback.

[P59]
Then again, he was used to people cowering the moment they heard the words *Fire King*. Aside from Cheongpung, this might be the first formidable opponent he’d encountered.

[P60]
*Anyway.*

[P61]
I scratched the back of my head and looked Sama Pyo up and down.

[P62]
“So. What brings you here?”

[P63]
“I have important business. If it’s all right with you, I’d rather discuss it inside.”

[P64]
“It’s not all right with me.”

[P65]
Sama Pyo shrugged.

[P66]
“I only asked to be polite, but you really are unusual. Do you have something against the unorthodox faction too?”

[P67]
“It’s not that, exactly……”

[P68]
Damn it. Put that way, I didn’t have much of an answer.

[P69]
We’d only met once, but he hadn’t made a particularly bad first impression. And I wasn’t some fanatic who went around shouting about wiping out the unorthodox faction and how great the orthodox faction was.

[P70]
Jeok Cheongang didn’t seem to feel much differently.

[P71]
“What are you two doing standing there? Falling for each other?”

[P72]
With Jeok Cheongang saying that, I had no good reason to keep Sama Pyo out. I jerked my chin toward him.

[P73]
“Damn it. Come in, then.”

[P74]
“Thank you. And thank you, Great Hero Jeok.”

[P75]
Sama Pyo entered with a polite bow. Jeok Cheongang nodded.

[P76]
“The young brat has some manners. Or did he inherit his father’s sly streak?”

[P77]
Sama Pyo paused, then smiled.

[P78]
“Probably the latter. So you remember my father.”

[P79]
“I’d forgotten him until I saw your face. You’re the spitting image of the Black Night King in his younger days.”

[P80]
Black Night King Sima Gong.

[P81]
Sama Pyo’s father, and the man who had built the Black Dragon Demon Gate into what it was today.

[P82]
His epithet made him sound like one of the Ten Kings, but according to Gung Gibang, he had nothing to do with them.

[P83]
*Just like the Green Forest Battle King, leader of the Green Forest Alliance, and the Escort King of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.*

[P84]
They were Supreme Peak masters whose martial prowess was beyond most people’s reach. That still wasn’t enough to make them part of the legend of the Ten Kings.

[P85]
The Black Night King was one of the greatest masters of the unorthodox faction and the Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate. He’d earned his epithet in much the same way.

[P86]
“Still……”

[P87]
Jeok Cheongang studied Sama Pyo, then frowned.

[P88]
“I didn’t know the Black Night King had a son so young.”

[P89]
“I have seven older brothers and nine older sisters. I’m the youngest.”

[P90]
“Hah. The Virility Saber King would weep if he heard that. So you’re the Young Sect Leader.”

[P91]
Sama Pyo’s eyes widened slightly.

[P92]
“I am, but how did you—”

[P93]
“Isn’t it obvious?”

[P94]
Jeok Cheongang snorted.

[P95]
“That’s exactly the sort of thing the Black Night King would do. If you had the talent, he wouldn’t care if all his other children were buried alive with him.”

[P96]
“……”

[P97]
“He hasn’t changed much, then. You could never tell what that man was thinking. Sly as a fox and cunning as a viper.”

[P98]
There he went, insulting the man’s father to his face. My heart swelled.

[P99]
The insult implied he recognized Sama Pyo’s talent, but it was still an insult. Before the dutiful son could take offense and start something, I cut in.

[P100]
“So what brings you here?”

[P101]
“……Hmm. Well.”

[P102]
Sama Pyo’s expression was hard to read. He reached inside his robe and took something out.

[P103]
Paper—a fairly expensive commodity in Murim. The words at the top caught my eye at once.

[P104]
> ★I Was a Nameless Foot Soldier, but in the Two Dragons Pavilion, I’m a Murim Hero?!★

[P105]
I stared at the sheet he’d laid on the table and rubbed my chin.

[P106]
“This looks familiar.”

[P107]
Sama Pyo gave a quiet laugh.

[P108]
“It would.”

[P109]
“I don’t know who came up with it, but they’re a genius.”

[P110]
“It’s rather bold, too.”

[P111]
Tap.

[P112]
Sama Pyo’s long finger came down on one part of the sheet: the recruitment requirements Hyuk Mujin had scrawled in his terrible handwriting. Of all the lines beneath them, he pointed to one in particular.

[P113]
> \# Gender and sect affiliation don’t matter

[P114]
“I especially like this part,” he said.

[P115]
“So?”

[P116]
“I’d like to apply. To the Two Dragons Pavilion.”

[P117]
I’d suspected as much, but hearing him say it still left me with mixed feelings.

[P118]
I thought for a moment, then clicked my tongue.

[P119]
“Why?”

[P120]
“The moment I heard the song, I knew. It’s exactly the place I’ve been looking for.”

[P121]
“Yeah. Bullshit.”

[P122]
That wasn’t even funny.

[P123]
The song promised a new era of success, more sects seeking you out, and a changed life. None of that applied to Sama Pyo.

[P124]
The Black Dragon Demon Gate was one of the three most powerful sects in the unorthodox martial world. Even if Sama Pyo hadn’t been its Young Sect Leader, being born the Black Night King’s son all but guaranteed him wealth and status.

[P125]
*And he wants to join the Two Dragons Pavilion?*

[P126]
No matter how many orthodox diehards waved picket signs in protest, Sama Pyo could secure himself a position in the Murim Alliance.

[P127]
I folded my arms and stared at him.

[P128]
“If this is a joke, it’s not funny.”

[P129]
“Fortunately, I’m serious.”

[P130]
“Cut the bullshit. What’s the real reason?”

[P131]
“The notice didn’t say I had to give one.”

[P132]
“Then get lost. I won’t see you out.”

[P133]
Sama Pyo shrugged as though he had no choice.

[P134]
“I thought joining the Two Dragons Pavilion might let me shed the label of the unorthodox faction.”

[P135]
“You don’t seem all that eager to shed it.”

[P136]
“Is that really how I seem?”

[P137]
“I don’t trust you.”

[P138]
“Fair enough. Then I’ll speak frankly.”

[P139]
“Go on. Unless you want the shit beaten out of you.”

[P140]
Sama Pyo gave a quiet laugh. Then his expression hardened.

[P141]
His low voice reached my ears.

[P142]
“I intend to use you for my own benefit. Depending on the circumstances, you could be useful to me in any number of ways.”

[P143]
A heavy silence fell.

[P144]
Even Taishan stopped chewing. Hyuk Mujin looked between Sama Pyo and me, his eyes wide.

[P145]
Then someone broke the silence.

[P146]
“What an interesting fellow.”

[P147]
Jeok Cheongang was watching Sama Pyo with an expression I couldn’t read. Was he amused or angry? He turned to me.

[P148]
“What do you think?”

[P149]
I considered it for a moment.

[P150]
“He makes quite an impression. I doubt this is his first interview.”

[P151]
“Will you take him?”

[P152]
“Hard to say.”

[P153]
Black Dragon Saber Sama Pyo. I couldn’t tell how much of what he’d said was a joke and how much he meant.

[P154]
But one thing was certain.

[P155]
*He’s interesting.*

[P156]
Tap. Tap.

[P157]
For a moment, the only sound was my fingers against the table. I gathered my thoughts and looked Sama Pyo straight in the eye.

[P158]
“Let’s make one thing clear first.”

[P159]
“By all means.”

[P160]
“If you try anything—”

[P161]
“Summary execution,” Sama Pyo said before I could finish. “I’ll remember.”

[P162]
“Huh. Straight to the point.”

[P163]
“It’s only natural. Are we done, then?”

[P164]
“You haven’t been accepted. I’m just considering you. Go home for today.”

[P165]
“Very well.”

[P166]
What the hell was he really after?

[P167]
I watched Sama Pyo and Taishan prepare to leave, my curiosity only growing. Then I remembered one important thing.

[P168]
“And one more thing.”

[P169]
“……?”

[P170]
“You’re paying for that guy’s food.”

[P171]
“……!”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

“Wow! Refreshments! Taishan thanks you for the food!”

[P54]
Thud! Crack!

The innkeeper was going to weep tears of blood.

[P56]

[P57]
“Have I lived too long?”

[P58]
Even Jeok Cheongang couldn’t help being taken aback.

[P59]

[P60]
*Anyway.*

[P61]
I scratched the back of my head and looked Sama Pyo up and down.

[P62]
“So. What brings you here?”

[P63]
“I have important business. If it’s all right with you, I’d rather discuss it inside.”

“It’s not all right with me.”

[P65]
Sama Pyo shrugged.

“I only asked to be polite, but you really are unusual. Do you have something against the unorthodox faction too?”

[P67]
“It’s not that, exactly……”

[P69]

Jeok Cheongang didn’t seem to feel much differently.

“What are you two doing standing there? Falling for each other?”

[P73]
“Damn it. Come in, then.”

[P74]
“Thank you. And thank you, Great Hero Jeok.”

[P75]

[P76]
“The young brat has some manners. Or did he inherit his father’s sly streak?”

[P77]
Sama Pyo paused, then smiled.

[P81]
Sama Pyo’s father, and the man who had built the Black Dragon Demon Gate into what it was today.

[P82]

[P83]
*Just like the Green Forest Battle King, leader of the Green Forest Alliance, and the Escort King of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.*

[P85]

[P86]
“Still……”

Jeok Cheongang studied Sama Pyo, then frowned.

[P88]

[P89]

[P90]

[P91]
Sama Pyo’s eyes widened slightly.

“……”

“So what brings you here?”

[P101]
“……Hmm. Well.”

[P102]

“This looks familiar.”

Sama Pyo gave a quiet laugh.

[P108]
“It would.”

“I don’t know who came up with it, but they’re a genius.”

[P110]
“It’s rather bold, too.”

Tap.

[P114]

[P115]
“So?”

[P116]
“I’d like to apply. To the Two Dragons Pavilion.”

[P117]

[P118]

[P119]
“Why?”

[P120]
“The moment I heard the song, I knew. It’s exactly the place I’ve been looking for.”

[P121]
“Yeah. Bullshit.”

[P122]

[P123]

[P124]

[P125]
*And he wants to join the Two Dragons Pavilion?*

[P126]

[P127]
I folded my arms and stared at him.

[P128]
“If this is a joke, it’s not funny.”

[P129]

[P132]

[P134]

[P135]
“You don’t seem all that eager to shed it.”

[P136]
“Is that really how I seem?”

[P137]
“I don’t trust you.”

[P138]
“Fair enough. Then I’ll speak frankly.”

[P139]
“Go on. Unless you want the shit beaten out of you.”

[P140]
Sama Pyo gave a quiet laugh. Then his expression hardened.

[P141]
His low voice reached my ears.

[P142]
“I intend to use you for my own benefit. Depending on the circumstances, you could be useful to me in any number of ways.”

[P143]
A heavy silence fell.

[P144]
Even Taishan stopped chewing. Hyuk Mujin looked between Sama Pyo and me, his eyes wide.

[P145]
Then someone broke the silence.

[P146]
“What an interesting fellow.”

[P147]

[P148]
“What do you think?”

[P149]
I considered it for a moment.

[P150]
“He makes quite an impression. I doubt this is his first interview.”

[P151]
“Will you take him?”

[P152]
“Hard to say.”

[P153]
Black Dragon Saber Sama Pyo. I couldn’t tell how much of what he’d said was a joke and how much he meant.

[P154]
But one thing was certain.

[P155]
*He’s interesting.*

[P156]
Tap. Tap.

[P158]
“Let’s make one thing clear first.”

[P159]
“By all means.”

[P160]
“If you try anything—”

[P161]
“Summary execution,” Sama Pyo said before I could finish. “I’ll remember.”

[P162]
“Huh. Straight to the point.”

[P163]
“It’s only natural. Are we done, then?”

[P164]
“You haven’t been accepted. I’m just considering you. Go home for today.”

[P165]
“Very well.”

[P166]
What the hell was he really after?

[P167]
I watched Sama Pyo and Taishan prepare to leave, my curiosity only growing. Then I remembered one important thing.

[P168]
“And one more thing.”

“……?”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
